A couple shops in Philly and NYC. Eventually I'll put in an order with Stephane at tea-masters.com

Yunnan Sourcing is a good store that specializes in puerh, but they have an amazing, but small selection of Chinese oolongs.

What-Cha is a relatively new store that focuses on unusual teas or teas from less established tea producing regions.

Crimson Lotus Tea is a small curated store specializing in puerh where everything is good.

White2Tea is a another small curated store that has quite a lot of good puerh.
What-cha for my loose tea plus they are based in the uk so quick postage
Whole Foods usually. My husband works there and can bring home broken containers for pretty cheap! I've gotten some from David's Tea before too and they have some pretty fun flavors.

I like Tea Guys. They don't sell accessories, just tea. But their pricing is competitive and you can get good pricing on samples. I usually try a few new samples when I order my regular teas in larger quantities.

I love Teavivre as well, and get a lot of my Chinese teas there. Aside from them, I go with Verdant Tea for the more obscure/special Chinese stuff, Den's Tea for my Japanese tea. I get my bulk English blacks from Golden Moon Tea, as well as their Masala Chai. Because multiple full pounds of tea is reasonable.

There was a hole in my heart when Butiki Teas closed, because they were my favorite for blends and infusions (like a cantaloupe cream Bai Mu Dan! and purple tea with blueberries!). I think I've finally found a replacement in Whispering Pines Tea--very unique stuff! I don't know how many other people think to use mushrooms in their blends (besides reishi dust, I suppose).

Mighty Leaf is my go-to online store. Their site has quite a selection.  

Red Blossom Tea is also very good for Chinese teas. I order from them very frequently.
